name: How to File a Mechanics Lien in STATE
description: Step-by-step guide to filing a mechanics lien in STATE, including the statutory filing deadline, recorder office, required documents, and enforcement steps.

step.name: Confirm your deadline clock has started
step.text: Identify your last day of furnishing labor or materials to the project. In most states the filing deadline runs from this date; in some it runs from project completion. The VoiceLogPro lien calculator computes the exact date for your state.

step.name: Send your preliminary notice (if required)
step.text: If STATE requires a preliminary notice (PRELIMINARY_NOTICE_RULE), send it before the deadline. Send by certified mail with return receipt for proof of service. Keep a copy.

step.name: Prepare the lien document (claim of lien / affidavit)
step.text: Your lien must include: your name and address, the property owner's name, a legal property description, the amount owed, and a description of the labor/materials furnished. In states like Texas the lien must be sworn and notarized.

step.name: Record the lien in the right county
step.text: Record the lien with the county recorder in the county where the property is located. Pay the recording fee (approximately $25-150 for the first page, varies by county).

step.name: Serve the lien on the owner and enforce (foreclose) within the deadline
step.text: Some states require you to serve a copy of the recorded lien on the owner within days of recording. Then enforce (foreclose) the lien within STATE's enforcement window (LIEN_ENFORCEMENT_RULE).

tool.name: Contemporaneous daily log (proof of last furnishing date)
